cause_quote: The new Darwin reader only bypassed the unreadable-arguments error when `executable && isForeignNativeExecutable(executable, uid) && native.isPlatformBinary(pid)` was true, so an unreadable third-party daemon or Apple `.app` service could abort the census.
user_saw: On affected Macs, `openclaw doctor --fix` reported that legacy plugin capture cleanup was skipped and left eligible directories on disk.
summary: Doctor now excludes unreadable foreign-UID processes from the legacy capture census, preserves foreign-owned legacy directories, and uses custody and installed-index references for managed native cleanup.
reasoning: The #154324 diff shows that Doctor previously only reported legacy captures and that the same commit introduced both automatic deletion and the Darwin census that could veto it. The later #157102 diff retained the executable and platform-signature checks for processes with a known UID, so the reported setup was blocked from the first version of automatic cleanup.
